about: The introit of the Third Sunday of Advent, from which the day takes its name of Gaudéte. The antiphon is the opening of the same Mass’s epistle, and the psalm verse the opening of its offertory: one Mass says the same thing three times, each time more fully.

seg.tr: Rejoice always in the Lord; once more I say, rejoice. Let all people know your modesty, for the Lord is at hand. Let nothing make you anxious, but in all prayer let your petitions become known before God.
You have blessed Your land, O Lord; You have turned away the captivity of Jacob.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

ex.w037: In the doxology the verb remains unspoken. Liturgical usage supplies the wish “glory be”.

seg.nr: After the doxology the Introit antiphon is repeated from Gaudéte to the psalm verse — by the choir at a sung Mass, by the priest himself at a low Mass.
